newsitem.title: INDIA: India call rates slip mildly at close, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: India call rates slip mildly at close, seen steady.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday at 4.50-4.75 percent, slightly lower from the opening rate of 5.0 percent, dealers said.
"Most of the deals were in the region of 4.50-5.00 percent," dealers said.
"The rates are likely rule easy on Wednesday, while some tightness if any will be seen in the next week," a dealer at state-run said.
"There will be only two working days in the next week on the eve of national holidays, which may put some pressure on call rates on Saturday," he said.
The market is expecting major inflow of funds on account of gilts coupon payments and through Reserve Bank of India (RBI) purchase of spot dollars in the forex market, dealers said.
A reduction in the notified amount of (RBI) weekly 91-day treasury bills auction to one billion rupees from five billion will also favour the liquidity, dealers said.
The securities market was dull on Tuesday, with little action in zero coupon bonds maturing in 1999, dealers said.
The voulmes on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) fell to 1.21 billion rupees, against previous 2.17 billion rupees, dealers said.
The treasury bills maturing in July 1997 were traded at steady yields of 9.75 percent and 9.77 percent, dealers said.
